proposed_intervals.note: All five numbered sections and the closing penalty/modification text. End = date of EO 6260, whose section 11 revokes EO 6111; EO 6260 states no separate effective date, so signing date used. Liabilities incurred before revocation are preserved by EO 6260's savings sentence.

rationale: No: EO 6111 (held APP mirror text, 20 April 1933) has five numbered sections, each running 'until further order' or being a standing licence/penalty provision, with no fixed term. EO 6260 of 28 August 1933 (held APP mirror text) section 11 provides: The Executive Orders of April 5, 1933, Forbidding the Hoarding of Gold Coin, Gold Bullion and Gold Certificates, and April 20, 1933, relating to Foreign Exchange and the Earmarking and Export of Gold Coin or Bullion or Currency, respectively, are hereby revoked. That names EO 6111 by date and subject and revokes all of it, so every clause (including section 3, which kept the 10 March 1933 foreign-exchange provisions in force, and section 4 licence entitlements) ended on 28 August 1933. Savings: section 11 preserves acts done, accrued rights and pending or past liabilities under the revoked orders; that preserves enforcement for pre-revocation conduct and does not keep any command in force. The held corpus has no earlier ending (cruden number search finds no other order citing EO 6111 by number). Proposal for independent review only.
